course_name_original: Values and Accountability in Computing and Artificial (FMFI.KAI/1-AIN-415/25)
course_name_en: Values and Accountability in Computing and Artificial Intelligence

learning_outcomes.text: Identify basic ethical issues related to the development and use of IT and AI technologies.
Apply ethical frameworks to analyze specific cases in computer science.
Understand the relationship between technology, values, and society.
Consider the impacts of IT and AI decisions on user privacy, responsibility for their data, and the transparency of the processes of those processing them.
Recognize dilemmas from the perspective of the different interests of different stakeholders.
Approach critically the design, use, and regulation of digital systems.

syllabus_topics: The role of ethics in IT and AI
Bias and fairness in AI systems
Societal impacts of informatization and artificial intelligence
Ethics of interaction: chatbots, assistants and social AI
Research ethics and academic integrity with a focus on the use of AI tools
Democracy, power and regulation in the age of AI

assessment_methods.method: final presentation of the selected topic

assessment_rules: The final assessment is based on 50% active participation in seminars and 50% a final presentation of a selected topic.
bibliography: Shannon Vallor (2016): Technology and the Virtues.
Batya Friedman, Peter H. Kahn Jr., Alan Borning (2006): Value Sensitive Design and Information Systems.
Selbst et al. (2019): Fairness and Abstraction in Sociotechnical Systems.
Binns, R. (2018): Fairness in Machine Learning: Lessons from Political Philosophy. Communications of the ACM.
institution: Univerzita Komenského v Bratislave (Comenius University Bratislava)
degree: Bachelor Applied Informatics (1-AIN), Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics
